title: Tribhuwan Shivhare v. State of U.P.
court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
coram: Surya Prakash Kesarwani, J.; Surendra Singh-I, J.
disposition: Writ disposed; liberty to file para 6.8 objection with stay of coercive action.
headnote: Without examining merits, a writ against a recovery certificate of Rs. 4,86,030 was disposed of by granting liberty to file an objection under Para 6.8 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 before the Executive Engineer, DVVNL Hamirpur, within four weeks, to be decided within the next four weeks after hearing, with coercive action stayed for eight weeks or until disposal of the objection, whichever is earlier.
facts: Tribhuwan Shivhare challenged a recovery certificate dated 18 June 2022 for Rs. 4,86,030, seeking certiorari to quash it and a mandamus restraining realization of that amount. The Executive Engineer, Dakshinanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Limited, Hamirpur was impleaded as respondent no. 5. Counsel for the distribution company stated on instructions that the petitioner may file an objection against the impugned demand, which would be decided in accordance with law within a time-bound period.

holding_units.topic: objection to recovery demand as alternate remedy
holding_units.holding: Without expressing any opinion on merits, a writ challenging a recovery certificate may be disposed of by granting liberty to submit an objection under Para 6.8 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 before the Executive Engineer, to be decided in accordance with law after reasonable opportunity of hearing, with a time-bound stay of coercive action pending that disposal.

principle_tags.application: Writ against a recovery certificate disposed of without a merits examination by relegating the consumer to an objection under Para 6.8 of the Supply Code before the Executive Engineer.

Petitioner given four weeks to file a Para 6.8 objection; the Executive Engineer to decide it within the next four weeks after hearing; coercive action stayed for eight weeks or until disposal, whichever is earlier.

not_decided.point: Merits of the recovery certificate dated 18.6.2022 and the demand of Rs. 4,86,030
not_decided.note: The Court expressly declined to express any opinion on the merits of the petitioner's case.
